Macrons

Consonantal i

Consonantal u

Theme

Money, work & business

commercial adjective

to do with trade; run for profit

also commercially, commercial venture, commercial city, trading port, for profit, business district

classical

Cic. Fin. 5.91: nec mercātūra quaestuōsa
Liv. 39.25: maritimum emporium … quaestuōsum et frūgiferum

quaestuōsus, quaestuōsa, quaestuōsum

profitable, money-making

What brings in money, from quaestus, gain (Lewis & Short): a commercial venture is rēs quaestuōsa. Of a person it means greedy for gain, and Plautus uses quaestuōsa of a prostitute (Mil. 3.1.190, old numbering; Lewis & Short), so say it of the business, not of the people in it. Where English “commercial” only means “of trade”, Latin uses the genitive: mercātūrae, negōtiōrum (see business).

Other words

  • emporium, emporiī n. — a commercial town, a trading port, a market

    noun, second declension · also used · classical · Liv. 39.25; M-O s.v. city (as commercial center), after Egger; Traupman 173

    From Greek; a place of trade, usually on the sea or a river (Lewis & Short).

  • mercātōrius, mercātōria, mercātōrium — of traders, merchant (ship)

    also used · classical · Plaut. Bacch. 2.3.2 (old numbering): nāvis mercātōria, a merchant ship (Lewis & Short)

    (vōx cōmica: Plaut.; in ōrātiōne solūtā rāra)

    Lewis & Short has it only from Plautus.

Examples

  • … ūnum maritimum emporium fuisse quondam Thessalīs quaestuōsum et frūgiferum

    … that it had once been the Thessalians’ one seaport, a profitable and productive place of tradeLiv. 39.25

See also business, merchant, profit, advertisement, economic.
